messages.subject: Modeling residual item covarance
parts:
Dear Phil,

Thank you for a great package. Really incredible! I am evaluating a unidimensional scale. Is there a way to model residual covariance of observed variables (e.g.,lavaan i1~~i2/COV=i1*i2)?

Best,
Rico

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Modeling residual item covarance
parts:
Hi Rico,

Categorical response data do not have residuals in the usual sense, because they are fully redundant with the expected values of the model. So, to impose any type of residual correlation you must express the relationship as another latent trait which loads only on the items which covary (in that sense, the new latent trait "explains" any correlation not explained by the primary dimension). 

For example, say that in a 5-item test like below, items 2 and 3 have residual correlations. Because there's only two loadings, the model will not be identified unless further constraints are imposed (e.g., equality constraints). 

`````
library(mirt)
dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
model <- "
    F1 = 1-5
    R23 = 2,3
    CONSTRAIN = (a2, 2,3)"
mod <- mirt(dat, model) 
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)
summary(mod)
````

If there are a lot of these residual covariance terms such that the dimensionality gets quite high, it may be better to reformulate the model with the bfactor() function. HTH.
      

Phil
